claims.text: As you arrive at this singular stop, Buttermilk & Bourbon, you'll encounter the culinary realm of Chef Jason Santos, a renowned innovator whose bold twist on Southern cuisine has captivated diners since the restaurant's 2017 inception.
As you step towards Buttermilk & Bourbon in Boston’s Back Bay, the tantalizing aroma of Southern spices mingled with the sweet, smoky scent of bourbon greets you.
This culinary haven, with its vibrant energy and inviting atmosphere, draws diners into the rich, flavorful world of New Orleans-inspired cuisine.
Opened in 2017, Buttermilk & Bourbon is the brainchild of Jason Santos, a renowned Boston-based chef and restaurateur.
Santos first captured national attention as the runner-up on Season 7 of Fox’s _Hell’s Kitchen_, where his blue hair and dynamic culinary style made him a standout.
His journey continued as he became the Blue Team Sous Chef under Gordon Ramsay and later appeared as a kitchen expert on Paramount's _Bar Rescue_.
These experiences have shaped his reputation as a creative force in the culinary world, seamlessly blending Southern comfort food with inventive flair.
At Buttermilk & Bourbon, guests can indulge in a menu that reflects Santos’ passion for Southern cuisine.
The restaurant offers a variety of dishes, such as crispy fried chicken and fluffy biscuits, all accentuated by the distinct flavors of Bourbon Street cocktails.
The ambiance mimics the lively spirit of New Orleans, making it a popular spot for both locals and visitors alike.
The location of Buttermilk & Bourbon also carries a historical note, as it sits near the site of the former Hotel Vendome.
This iconic hotel was the first in Boston to be fully lit by electric light, thanks to an independent electrical lighting plant designed by Thomas Edison in 1882.
claims.evidence: In 1882, the Hotel Vendome installed an independent electrical lighting plant designed by Thomas Edison, making it the first commercial hotel in Boston to be completely lit by electric light.

claims.text: However, it was also the site of a tragic event on June 17, 1972, when a four-alarm fire led to the collapse of the building’s southeast corner, resulting in the loss of nine Boston firefighters.
This poignant history adds a layer of depth to the vibrant surroundings of Buttermilk & Bourbon.
To experience Chef Jason Santos’ culinary magic, reservations are required, and the restaurant welcomes diners from Tuesday to Sunday, with meals typically priced under $30.
Whether you’re seeking the warmth of Southern hospitality or the excitement of innovative cuisine, Buttermilk & Bourbon promises a memorable dining adventure.
